exodus.7.p1.b1.text: See, I have made you like God to Pharaoh, and your brother Aaron will be your prophet.

exodus.7.p1.b2.text: You are to speak all that I command you, and your brother Aaron is to tell Pharaoh to let the Israelites go out of his land.

exodus.7.p1.b3.text: Pharaoh will not listen to you. Then I will lay My hand on Egypt, and by mighty acts of judgment I will bring the divisions of My people the Israelites out of the land of Egypt.

exodus.7.p1.b4.text: Moses was eighty years old and Aaron was eighty-three when they spoke to Pharaoh.

exodus.7.p2.b6.text: Take your staff and throw it down before Pharaoh … it will become a serpent.

exodus.7.p2.b7.text: Aaron threw his staff down before Pharaoh and his officials, and it became a serpent.

exodus.7.p3.b8.text: But Pharaoh called the wise men and sorcerers and magicians of Egypt, and they also did the same things by their magic arts.

exodus.7.p3.b9.text: Each one threw down his staff, and it became a serpent …

exodus.7.p3.b10.text: But Aaron’s staff swallowed up the other staffs.

exodus.7.p3.b11.text: Still, Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he would not listen to them, just as the LORD had said.

exodus.7.p4.b12.text: Go to Pharaoh in the morning as you see him walking out to the water. Wait on the bank of the Nile to meet him, and take in your hand the staff that was changed into a snake.

exodus.7.p4.b13.text: The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, has sent me to tell you: Let My people go, so that they may worship Me in the wilderness. But you have not listened until now.

exodus.7.p4.b14.text: This is what the LORD says: By this you will know that I am the LORD. Behold, with the staff in my hand I will strike the water of the Nile, and it will turn to blood.

exodus.7.p4.b15.text: The fish in the Nile will die, the river will stink, and the Egyptians will be unable to drink its water.’”

exodus.7.p5.b16.text: Take your staff and stretch out your hand over the waters of Egypt … that they may become blood.

exodus.7.p5.b17.text: … in the presence of Pharaoh and his officials, Aaron raised the staff and struck the water of the Nile, and all the water was turned to blood.

exodus.7.p6.b18.text: The fish in the Nile died, and the river smelled so bad that the Egyptians could not drink its water. And there was blood throughout the land of Egypt.

exodus.7.p6.b19.text: But the magicians of Egypt did the same things by their magic arts. So Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he would not listen to Moses and Aaron …

exodus.7.p6.b20.text: Instead, Pharaoh turned around, went into his palace, and did not take any of this to heart.

exodus.7.p7.b21.text: So all the Egyptians dug around the Nile for water to drink, because they could not drink the water from the river.

exodus.7.p7.b22.text: And seven full days passed after the LORD had struck the Nile.
